acceptedWorkstreams.title: Define what "activated in 48 hours" means and measure it, then write the emails around the drop-off points

Find where new educators stop, then write the five emails around those drop-off points, each with one call to action pointing at the exact screen and checked against the live app.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Sign up as a new educator, record every email the product sends today, then write only the emails that are missing
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Create a fresh educator account on the live product and log every email it sends in the first 48 hours: subject, sender, time after the action, and what it asks the person to do. Map those against the four activation steps in the goal (set up workspace, create a channel, schedule a Buzz call, post course files) and list which step has no email. Deliver the log, the gap map and drafts of the missing emails only, so nothing duplicates what is already sent. Tasks: email log and gap map (research), drafts for the gaps (content).

pendingIdeas.title: Define what stops the sequence, so active users do not keep getting onboarding mail
pendingIdeas.description: The fastest way to lose a new educator is to send them a fifth "get started" email after they have already run a session. Work: write the suppression rules (first cohort created, first call held, unsubscribe, plan enquiry, account inactive for thirty days) and what each rule does to the remaining emails. Deliver the suppression table, the one state that is ambiguous today, and a test plan with seeded accounts for the three most likely orders of events.

upvotes.reason: Suppression rules prevent onboarding mail landing on already-active users, which is a real trust cost.

pendingIdeas.title: Give each email one action, and put that action in the subject line
pendingIdeas.description: A welcome sequence that asks for setup, a call and a file upload in one message gets none of them. Work: assign one action per email, name it in the subject ("Create your first channel"), and cut everything else to a single line of context and one link. Deliver the five subjects, the one-action rule, and the check that no email contains two buttons pointing at different tasks.

upvotes.reason: One action per email with that action in the subject is a clear, testable rule.

pendingIdeas.title: Pick the one email to test first from the biggest drop-off, not from the start of the sequence
pendingIdeas.description: Teams test email one because it is first, then learn nothing about where users actually stop. Work: using the activation definition the team already agreed, find the step where most new educators stop, and choose the email that sits at that step for the first experiment, with one change (subject, action or timing) and a stated success measure. Deliver the drop-off evidence, the chosen email, the hypothesis and the sample size needed before the result means anything.

upvotes.reason: Choosing the first test from the biggest drop-off rather than email one is methodologically right.

pendingIdeas.title: Trigger on what the user has done, not on days since sign-up, and say what happens if they are ahead
pendingIdeas.description: A fixed Day 0/2/4 sequence mails "create your first channel" to someone who created three yesterday. Work: define the state each email assumes and the condition that sends it (no channel yet, no invite sent, no session scheduled), plus the skip rule when the user is ahead and the stop rule when activation is reached. Deliver the state table, the trigger conditions, and the one sequence step that has no reliable signal today, with what it would take to get one.

upvotes.reason: Behaviour-triggered emails with skip rules beat a fixed day sequence for real users.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the plain-text version and the send-time rule, because HTML email on a Nigerian mobile connection is a hidden cost
pendingIdeas.description: Heavy templates with web fonts and large images arrive slowly or not at all, and an email sent at 3am local time is read late or never. Work: produce each email as a plain-text variant with no image dependency, set the send window by recipient time zone, and define quiet hours. Deliver the text versions, the timing rule, and the measured size of the current templates if they exist, since size is the part a reader can verify.

upvotes.reason: A plain-text variant and a time-zone send window is a practical cost fix for Nigerian mobile connections.
